To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the accuracy of a model generated by a commercial data mining tool improves with the size of the sample, but at a decreasing rate, and that a model based on 10,000 or more records is likely to achieve 95 percent of the accuracy of the theoretical model based on an infinite sample.
the accuracy of decision tree-based data mining models is a decreasing function of sample size and that the relationship is well approximated by a power function.

the accuracy of decision-tree based data mining models improves at a decreasing pace with increasing sample size, and the rate of accuracy improvement decreases with increasing sample size; and that the accuracy of models based on samples of approximately 10,000 data records is within 0.1 percent of the accuracy of models using all data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the accuracy of sample based models.
the accuracy of models generated by data mining tools using progressively larger sample sizes.
the accuracy and efficiency of sample based decision-tree models and the impact of sample size on the predictive accuracy of such models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sample based model accuracy approximating the model accuracy of a full data set model can be achieved with a sample size of approximately 10,000.
, in the case of the two data mining packages tested, the sample based models had predictive accuracies approximating those of models based on the full dataset.
the sample based model accuracy is within 0.2 percent of the expected accuracy of the model based on all available records.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the results suggest that sample based modeling can be an attractive alternative for very large datasets provided that a sufficient sample size is chosen and that the sample is chosen in such a way that the sample is representative of the population.
the accuracy of a decision-tree based data mining model can be approximated by a power curve that is fitted across a progressive sample of the data.
the sample size for a decision tree model can be estimated by a power curve, which is a function of the number of records and the accuracy of the model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accuracy of decision tree models can be approximated with reasonable accuracy by using only 10 percent or less of the available data.
sample based models can be very useful for modeling large datasets, and the sample size required for an adequate sample based model is not as large as many might have expected.
the accuracy of sample based models is very close to that of the theoretical infinite sample model, and therefore sample based models are a viable alternative to models built on all available data.
